title: Compass and Atlas
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Veldenmark, Casper Iversen carries diplomatic codes between a collapsing capital and the neutral port of Havnvik, trusted because she is nobody. When a sealed letter entrusted to her reveals that the family sheltering her — the ambassador's household, the closest thing she has to kin — is marked for elimination by the faction seizing power, she discovers the evacuation ship has only one berth left beyond her own. Torn between the ambassador's daughter Ilse, who has become her dearest friend and something more, and the old ambassador himself, whose death would end any hope of a restored republic, Casper must decide what loyalty means when every choice betrays someone. In the end she forges a third path: she gives up her own berth, sends Ilse and her father together under one name, and stays behind as witness — surviving the purge to carry the republic's true history out of the country in spring.
about_author: Astrid Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private correspondence of displaced diplomats. She writes from a farmhouse on the Baltic coast, where the winter light reminds her of letters that never arrived.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Opening in occupied Veldenmark's capital, Casper delivers coded dispatches through checkpoints, establishing her rules of silence and her careful invisibility. She arrives at Ambassador Brandt's frostbitten residence and is quietly folded into the household's dwindling warmth. Emotional beat: longing for belonging disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: Household of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Winter deepens; she maps the household — pragmatic Ambassador Brandt, sharp-tongued Ilse, the loyal cook Marta, young clerk Tomas — and begins, against her own rules, to care. A first coded warning arrives: names are being collected in the capital. Emotional beat: found family taking shape while danger gathers at the edges.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse intercepts a sealed letter meant only for her father and reads it: the family is named in a purge list, and a neutral ship will call at Havnvik with limited berths. She hides it, torn between protecting her father and confessing. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper learns Ilse knows, and the two women circle each other — suspicion giving way to confession by candlelight, and the first admission of feeling neither can act on. They agree to tell no one, not even the ambassador. Emotional beat: love declared in the grammar of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Berths
chapters.summary: Ambassador Brandt's POV. The ambassador privately confirms there is one berth beyond Casper's official passage. He drafts two versions of his own farewell — one in which he leaves, one in which he stays — and burns both. Emotional beat: a father measuring his life against his daughter's future.

chapters.title: Havnvik Road
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The household travels toward the port under false papers; a checkpoint nearly unravels them until Casper spends a code-phrase she was never authorized to spend, burning part of her own safety. Tomas sees what it cost her. Emotional beat: sacrifice performed without applause.

chapters.title: The Faction's Offer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A former colleague, now serving the new regime, finds Casper in Havnvik and offers her immunity and a berth home if she surrenders the ambassador's cipher books — proof enough to hang him legally rather than violently. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy; corruption wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: One Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The ship signals departure within hours. Ilse discovers her father intends to give her the berth and stay; she confronts him, and he refuses to argue — he simply hands her the decision, saying a courier should know how to choose. Casper must finally say which name goes on the manifest. Emotional beat: the novel's moral fulcrum, love and duty colliding.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, climax. At the quay, Casper forges the manifest: one berth under a dead cousin's name, given to father and daughter jointly, and strikes her own passage. The regime's men close in; Marta and Tomas create the diversion that lets the Brandts board. Casper and Ilse part with an unspoken promise. Emotional beat: heartbreak chosen deliberately, agency over fate.

chapters.title: What Survives the Winter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, resolution. Months later, hiding in Havnvik's archive district with Marta and Tomas as her new household, Casper copies the republic's true record into cipher of her own making. Spring brings a smuggled letter from Ilse — alive, waiting — and a route out. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; found family enduring, and love deferred but not destroyed.
